modelAnswer:
The bar chart illustrates the total volume of express parcels delivered in China from 2021 to 2026. Overall, the figure rose steadily throughout the period, climbing from 108.3 billion parcels in 2021 to an estimated 163.0 billion in 2026, which represents a total growth of roughly 50 percent.

In 2021, the volume stood at 108.3 billion parcels. It then grew at a moderate pace to 116.8 billion in 2022 and 126.5 billion in 2023, with an annual increase of around 8 percent. Growth accelerated in the following years: the figure climbed to 138.0 billion in 2024 and 150.2 billion in 2025, and it is projected to reach 163.0 billion in 2026. For instance, the increase between 2023 and 2024 alone amounted to 11.5 billion parcels, larger than the annual total of many European countries.

Several factors account for this impressive growth. First, online shopping has become a daily habit for most Chinese consumers, and e-commerce platforms constantly create fresh demand through promotions and new services. Second, improved logistics networks and the wider use of intelligent sorting and delivery systems have raised efficiency and lowered costs. Third, rural e-commerce has expanded quickly, bringing millions of new customers into the market. In addition, the boom of livestream shopping and same-day delivery services has further stimulated consumption, as people can now receive goods within hours of placing an order.

In my view, the express delivery industry will keep expanding, although the growth rate may gradually slow down as the market matures. Companies should invest in green packaging, better working conditions and higher pay for couriers, and wider use of unmanned delivery vehicles. I believe that by 2030 the annual volume will exceed 200 billion parcels, and China will remain the world's largest delivery market. To sustain this growth, the industry must shift its focus from speed to quality and sustainability.

Second, the government has set ambitious carbon targets and offered subsidies and tax incentives for clean energy projects. Third, technological progress has improved the efficiency of solar cells, allowing more electricity to be generated from the same area. In addition, growing demand for green energy from factories and households has pushed investment higher.

In my opinion, solar power will continue to grow rapidly in the coming years, because it is now cheaper than coal power in many regions. However, challenges remain, such as grid absorption, energy storage and the recycling of old panels. The government should invest more in storage facilities and smart grids so that clean electricity can be used efficiently, and the falling price of storage batteries will make solar energy more reliable around the clock. If these problems are solved, I predict that China will add over 200 GW of solar capacity each year by 2030, greatly speeding up the transition to a low-carbon economy.

The recovery can be explained by several factors. First, as the economy reopened, commuting, business travel and tourism all returned to normal. Second, ride-hailing has become cheaper and more convenient thanks to fierce competition among platforms, which has attracted more users. Third, the development of electric vehicles has reduced operating costs for drivers, allowing the industry to expand quickly. Fourth, elderly people and residents of small cities have begun to use these services more frequently, expanding the user base.

In my opinion, ride-hailing will remain a major part of urban transport, but its growth may slow as the market becomes saturated. Platforms should pay more attention to driver welfare and service quality rather than simply cutting prices. The government, for its part, should strengthen safety supervision and data protection. I predict that daily orders will exceed 40 million by 2027, and more vehicles in the industry will be electric and intelligent, which will not only reduce emissions but also lower costs for both drivers and passengers.

The pie chart shows how Chinese domestic tourists spent their money in 2024. Overall, accommodation, transport and dining together accounted for nearly three quarters of total tourist spending, while shopping and other items made up a relatively small proportion.

In other words, roughly seven out of every ten yuan spent by tourists went to accommodation, transport and food. These figures suggest that tourists today care more about comfortable stays and convenient travel than about buying souvenirs.

The structure of tourist spending reflects several recent changes. First, as incomes rise, travellers are willing to pay more for better hotels and faster transport such as high-speed rail and flights. Second, the popularity of food tourism has made local cuisine a major attraction, which explains why dining takes up almost a quarter of spending. Third, the small share of shopping suggests that tourists are shifting from material purchases to experiences, a sign of a more mature tourism market.

In my view, tourism operators should adjust their products to match this spending pattern. Hotels should improve service quality, and cities should develop distinctive food and cultural programmes rather than relying on low-price group tours. Meanwhile, better transport links, such as new high-speed rail lines, will make short trips more frequent, further boosting spending on travel and dining. I predict that spending on entertainment and cultural experiences will grow in the future, while the share of shopping will continue to decline. If destinations can offer truly unique experiences, they will attract more repeat visitors and earn much higher revenue per visitor.

In other words, more AI jobs were created between 2023 and 2025 than in the entire first three years of the period combined.

This explosion of demand can be attributed to several factors. Second, the rise of generative AI since 2023 has encouraged almost every industry to recruit engineers, data scientists and algorithm specialists. Third, government policies treat AI as a strategic industry, and large amounts of investment have flowed into related companies. At the same time, the shortage of qualified workers has pushed companies to compete fiercely for talent, driving up salaries and openings.

From my point of view, the demand for AI professionals will remain strong, but the skills required will change rapidly. Universities and vocational colleges should update their courses to include machine learning, data analysis and AI ethics. Job seekers should combine technical ability with knowledge of a specific industry, because pure programming skills will not be enough. Companies, for their part, should strengthen internal training to develop their own talent instead of relying only on external hiring. I predict that by 2028 the total number of AI job openings will exceed 1.2 million, and the shortage of experienced talent will become the biggest challenge for the industry.

Colleges should continue to align their courses with industry needs, especially in advanced manufacturing, green energy and digital services. modelAnswer:
The pie chart compares different methods used to deal with urban household waste in China in 2024. Overall, incineration for power generation was the dominant method, accounting for more than half of all waste treated, while landfill played a much smaller role than in the past.

Specifically, incineration with power generation accounted for 55 percent of the total, making it by far the most common approach. Sanitary landfill ranked second with 20 percent, followed by recycling at 12 percent and composting or biochemical treatment at 8 percent. Other methods, such as temporary storage, made up the remaining 5 percent. Together, incineration and landfill handled three quarters of all municipal waste. It is worth noting that the share of recycling, at 12 percent, remains below the level of many developed countries, indicating considerable room for improvement.

This structure reflects a clear shift in China's waste management strategy. Landfill used to be the main method because it was cheap, but it occupies valuable land and produces unpleasant smells and greenhouse gases. In contrast, waste-to-energy plants can reduce the volume of waste dramatically and generate electricity at the same time. The growing proportion of incineration is therefore the result of stricter environmental rules, rising waste volumes and improvements in emission control technology.

In my view, the proportion of incinerated waste will continue to rise in the near future, while landfill will decline further. However, burning waste is not the final answer; recycling should be expanded, since it saves resources and energy. Citizens also need to develop the habit of sorting waste at home, which is the foundation of the whole system. The government should promote waste sorting more strictly and invest in advanced recycling facilities. I predict that by 2030, recycling will account for at least 20 percent of waste treatment, helping China move towards a truly green and circular economy.

Fourth, the success of events such as marathons and city cycling tours has created a strong sporting atmosphere across the country.

In my view, the proportion will keep increasing, but the pace depends on how well facilities serve ordinary people. Local governments should open more school playgrounds to the public and add fitness equipment in residential areas. Employers could also encourage staff to exercise by offering flexible working hours and gym subsidies. What is more, smart devices such as sports watches make it easier for people to monitor their activity and stay motivated. In my opinion, the cost structure will change gradually in the coming years. The share of labour costs should decline as automation spreads, while spending on information technology and green packaging is likely to rise. Companies should therefore keep upgrading their networks and equipment, and better route planning powered by artificial intelligence can cut fuel use and emissions significantly. I predict that by 2030 the proportion of transport costs will fall below 35 percent, and the industry will become both more efficient and more environmentally friendly.

chart.title: 2019—2024 年我国单位 GDP 二氧化碳排放量

tips: 描述时应突出逐年下降的趋势与降幅变化；分析可从能源结构、产业升级与碳市场三方面展开；结尾给出减排前景预测。
modelAnswer:
The bar chart shows the carbon dioxide emitted per 10,000 yuan of GDP in China from 2019 to 2024. Overall, the carbon intensity of the economy declined steadily, falling from 0.95 tonnes to 0.73 tonnes over the six years.

In 2019, each 10,000 yuan of GDP was associated with 0.95 tonnes of CO2 emissions. The figure dropped to 0.89 in 2020, 0.84 in 2021 and 0.80 in 2022, a fall of roughly 5 percent per year. The decline continued at a slightly slower pace in 2023 and 2024, when the figure reached 0.76 and 0.73 tonnes respectively. In total, carbon intensity fell by about 23 percent during the period. This means that the economy is becoming noticeably cleaner even as it continues to grow, which is exactly what sustainable development requires.

This positive trend results from several factors. First, the share of coal in the energy mix has decreased, while wind, solar and nuclear power have expanded rapidly. Second, factories have upgraded their equipment to use energy more efficiently, and many old, polluting plants have been closed. Third, the service industry, which produces more value with less energy, has grown faster than heavy industry. In addition, a nationwide carbon trading market now puts a price on emissions, encouraging companies to save energy. Together, these changes mean that China can produce more wealth while emitting less carbon.

From my point of view, the downward trend will continue, but the hardest part lies ahead, because the easiest improvements have already been made. The government should accelerate the construction of renewable energy projects and promote low-carbon technologies in steel, cement and transport. Companies should treat emission reduction as an opportunity to cut costs rather than a burden. I predict that carbon intensity will fall to around 0.60 tonnes by 2030, keeping China on track for its carbon neutrality goal.

The pie chart illustrates the channels through which Chinese companies hired new employees in 2024. Overall, online recruitment platforms were by far the most important channel, accounting for nearly half of all hires.

Specifically, online platforms such as job websites and mobile apps accounted for 46 percent of recruitment, the largest share by a wide margin. Campus recruitment came second with 21 percent, while employee referrals contributed 16 percent. Headhunters and professional agencies made up 9 percent of hires, and other channels, including job fairs and newspapers, represented the remaining 8 percent. Together, online and campus channels accounted for about two thirds of all new employees. It is worth noting that the share of traditional channels has shrunk dramatically, as printed advertisements have almost disappeared from the market.

The dominance of online recruitment reflects the digitalization of the labour market. Online platforms allow companies to reach millions of candidates quickly and at low cost, while job seekers can compare positions and salaries easily. The growing share of employee referrals also shows that companies value trusted recommendations, as referred workers often stay longer and perform better. Campus recruitment remains important because it gives employers access to fresh graduates with up-to-date knowledge. Moreover, social media and short-video platforms have become new channels for both employers and candidates, blurring the line between recruitment and marketing.

In my opinion, online recruitment will keep growing as artificial intelligence improves matching between jobs and candidates. However, companies should not rely on a single channel, since some skilled and experienced workers are found more easily through referrals or agencies. Job seekers, for their part, should build complete online profiles and maintain professional networks. At the same time, regulators should protect users' personal data on recruitment platforms, which has become a growing concern. I predict that by 2028, online platforms will account for more than half of all recruitment, and video interviews will become standard practice.

modelAnswer:
The pie chart shows how urban residents in China travelled to work every day in 2024. Overall, private cars and rail transit were the two leading commuting modes, together accounting for more than half of all trips.

Specifically, private cars ranked first, accounting for 27 percent of commuting trips, closely followed by rail transit such as metro systems at 24 percent. Public buses carried 18 percent of commuters, while electric bicycles accounted for 17 percent, showing their popularity for short journeys. Walking and cycling made up 9 percent of trips, and ride-hailing services represented the smallest share at 5 percent. In total, public transport, including rail and bus, served 42 percent of commuters. In other words, more than nine out of every ten commuters relied on some form of motorised transport, while only 9 percent walked or cycled.

This distribution reflects the rapid development of urban transport in China. The expansion of metro networks has given millions of people a fast and reliable alternative to cars, which explains the high proportion of rail travel. At the same time, electric bicycles remain attractive because they are cheap, flexible and unaffected by traffic jams. The relatively small share of ride-hailing suggests that most residents treat it as an occasional choice rather than a daily habit. Moreover, the growth of shared bicycles has made the last kilometre between station and office much easier, further supporting green commuting.

In my view, cities should continue to invest in rail transit and improve bus services, because shifting commuters from private cars to public transport is the most effective way to reduce congestion and emissions. The government could also build more dedicated lanes for buses and bicycles, and encouraging more walking and cycling would bring clear health benefits and reduce pressure on roads during peak hours. I predict that the share of rail transit will rise to around 30 percent by 2030, while the proportion of private car commuting will decline slightly as more metro lines open.

modelAnswer:
The bar chart displays the tourism revenue earned during the May Day holiday in China from 2019 to 2024. Overall, revenue fluctuated sharply in the first half of the period and then recovered strongly, reaching a new peak in 2024.

In 2019, the holiday generated 116.2 billion yuan in tourism revenue. The figure collapsed to just 46.8 billion in 2020, when the pandemic almost halted travel. It then rebounded to 113.8 billion in 2021, but fell back to 65.6 billion in 2022 due to renewed restrictions. The recovery accelerated from 2023, when revenue jumped to 146.5 billion, and it rose further to 167.0 billion in 2024, more than three times the level of 2020. This V-shaped pattern is one of the clearest examples of how external shocks can hit and then release consumer demand.

The sharp fluctuations clearly mirror the impact of the pandemic and the recovery afterwards. Once travel restrictions were lifted, pent-up demand was released, and people rushed to visit popular destinations. Rising incomes and the development of high-speed rail have also made travel easier and more affordable. In addition, local governments and tourism platforms promoted new products such as city walks, food tours and rural stays, which attracted a wider range of visitors. As a result, even a five-day holiday now makes a substantial contribution to the annual revenue of the tourism industry.

In my opinion, the strong rebound shows the vitality of China's tourism market, but it also creates pressure on popular scenic spots. Destinations should spread visitors across more days and areas, improve reservation systems and strengthen safety management. At the same time, the industry should develop more cultural and countryside tourism products to ease the crowding in famous cities. Moreover, better services for elderly and family travellers will open up new sources of growth for the whole industry. I predict that May Day tourism revenue will exceed 200 billion yuan by 2027, and domestic travel will remain the backbone of the market.

tips: 先总述采用率的快速攀升；重点分析 2023 年后加速的原因；结尾预测普及趋势并指出应用中的注意事项。
modelAnswer:
The line chart illustrates the proportion of Chinese companies that have adopted artificial intelligence technology between 2020 and 2025. Overall, the adoption rate rose sharply, increasing from 8.4 percent to 38.6 percent over the six years.

In 2020, fewer than one in ten companies, 8.4 percent, used AI in their business. The rate then climbed steadily to 12.1 percent in 2021 and 16.8 percent in 2022. Growth accelerated significantly from 2023 onwards: the figure jumped to 23.5 percent in 2023, 30.9 percent in 2024 and an estimated 38.6 percent in 2025. In other words, within just three years, the number of AI-using companies more than doubled. Moreover, the gap between large firms and small firms has narrowed, although big companies still lead the way. This means AI has spread from large corporations to a wide range of ordinary businesses.

This rapid spread can be explained by several factors. First, the cost of AI tools has fallen dramatically, making them affordable even for small firms. Second, the success of generative AI since 2023 has shown companies that the technology can save time in writing, design, customer service and coding. Third, competitive pressure has pushed firms to adopt AI, because those that use it can cut costs and respond to customers faster than their rivals. Finally, government support and cloud computing services have made adoption technically easier.

From my perspective, the adoption rate will continue to rise, but the challenge will shift from whether to use AI to how to use it well. Companies should train their employees, protect customer data and monitor the quality of AI outputs. Small businesses, in particular, need affordable and simple AI solutions. At the same time, clear rules and standards will be needed to ensure that AI is used fairly and responsibly. I predict that by 2028 more than 60 percent of Chinese companies will use AI in some form, and the technology will become as common as the internet is today.

modelAnswer:
The pie chart shows the destinations of graduates from higher vocational colleges in China in 2024. Overall, direct employment was the most common choice, accounting for nearly 60 percent of all graduates.

Specifically, 58 percent of vocational graduates entered the workforce directly, the largest share by far. Further study at undergraduate level, known as upgrading to a bachelor's degree, came second with 22 percent. Starting their own business accounted for 4 percent of graduates, and joining the military represented 3 percent. The remaining 13 percent were still looking for jobs or taking other paths, such as preparing for exams or further training. In total, about 80 percent of graduates either found a job or continued their education immediately after graduation.

These figures reveal several trends. First, the high proportion of direct employment reflects the practical, job-oriented nature of vocational education and the strong demand for skilled workers in manufacturing and services. In fact, many employers report that they prefer vocational graduates for technical positions because of their hands-on training. Second, the growing share of students continuing to study for a bachelor's degree, now more than one in five, shows that vocational graduates are increasingly ambitious and eager to improve their qualifications. Third, the relatively small share of self-employment suggests that starting a business remains difficult for young graduates without enough capital and experience.

In my opinion, vocational colleges should support students on every path. For those entering the job market, colleges should strengthen cooperation with companies and provide better career guidance. For those continuing their studies, smoother transfer programmes should be offered. The government could also provide start-up funds and mentoring for graduates who wish to create their own businesses. I predict that the proportion of students pursuing a bachelor's degree will rise to 30 percent by 2030, while direct employment will remain the dominant choice.

tips: 双系列柱状图要注意对比两组数据的差距及差距变化；分析原因可从政策力度与资源投入展开；结尾提出缩小差距的建议。
modelAnswer:
The bar chart compares the coverage rate of household waste sorting in pilot cities and ordinary prefecture-level cities in China from 2019 to 2024. Overall, both groups made steady progress, but pilot cities maintained a clear lead throughout the period.

In 2019, waste sorting covered 65 percent of pilot cities but only 30 percent of ordinary cities, a gap of 35 percentage points. Pilot cities improved to 71 percent in 2020, 76 percent in 2021, 82 percent in 2022, 86 percent in 2023 and 90 percent in 2024. Ordinary cities progressed more slowly at first, reaching 38 percent in 2020 and 45 percent in 2021, but then accelerated to 55 percent in 2022, 62 percent in 2023 and 68 percent in 2024. Although the gap narrowed to 22 percentage points by 2024, it remained considerable.

The contrast between the two groups reflects the role of policy and resources. Pilot cities received strong government support, clear regulations and sufficient funding for bins, vehicles and treatment plants, so their coverage rose quickly. Ordinary cities started later, with weaker awareness among residents and fewer facilities, which explains their slower progress. The acceleration after 2021 shows that nationwide campaigns and legal requirements have gradually spread from large cities to smaller ones.

In my view, closing the gap should be the next priority. The government should share the experience of pilot cities, subsidise sorting facilities in smaller cities and strengthen publicity in communities. Schools and media also play a key role in teaching people how to sort waste correctly. Without such efforts, the waste treated in one city would continue to pollute the environment of the whole region. I predict that by 2030, coverage in ordinary cities will exceed 85 percent, and the gap with pilot cities will almost disappear, creating the foundation for a nationwide circular economy.

tips: 双系列折线图应对比两条线的走向差异；分析线上崛起与线下波动的各自原因；结尾展望线上线下融合的发展趋势。
modelAnswer:
The line chart compares the number of offline gym members and online fitness users in China from 2019 to 2024. Overall, the two indicators moved in very different directions: gym membership fluctuated, while online fitness grew explosively.

In 2019, gym membership stood at 68.12 million, while online fitness had 185 million users. Gym membership rose slowly to 70.29 million in 2020 and 75.13 million in 2021, but then dropped to 71.08 million in 2022 and 69.85 million in 2023 before recovering to 72.4 million in 2024. In sharp contrast, online fitness users soared from 185 million in 2019 to 245 million in 2020, 320 million in 2021, 385 million in 2022, 410 million in 2023 and 442 million in 2024. By the end of the period, online users outnumbered gym members by roughly six to one.

The contrast has clear causes. During the pandemic, gyms were repeatedly closed, which pushed many people to exercise at home and damaged confidence in prepaid gym memberships. Even after reopening, high fees and inconvenient locations limited the recovery of traditional gyms. Online platforms, meanwhile, offer cheap or free classes that people can follow anytime and anywhere, supported by smart devices that track progress. Many users also enjoy the social features of live classes and the feeling of belonging to an online community.

In my opinion, the two forms of fitness will coexist rather than replace each other. Gyms should lower prices, offer flexible short-term memberships and combine offline coaching with online content. Online platforms should improve course quality and prevent injuries through better guidance. After all, face-to-face guidance and specialised equipment still offer value that screens cannot provide. I predict that online fitness users will easily exceed 600 million by the year 2030, while well-run gyms will survive by becoming more professional, social and community-oriented.

tips: 重点对比自驾游与团队游的差距扩大趋势；分析时可联系汽车普及、乡村道路改善与游客偏好变化；结尾对乡村旅游设施与服务提出建议。
modelAnswer:
The bar chart compares the number of self-driving tourists and group tourists visiting rural areas in China from 2019 to 2024. Overall, self-driving trips dominated rural tourism and grew strongly, while group travel recovered more slowly and remained far behind.

In 2019, rural areas received 1.65 billion self-driving visitors, almost twice the 0.86 billion group tourists. Both figures fell in 2020, to 1.12 billion and 0.34 billion respectively, but self-driving recovered quickly, reaching 1.98 billion in 2021 and 2.24 billion in 2022. Group tourism, by contrast, stayed weak, recovering only to 0.72 billion in 2021 and slipping to 0.58 billion in 2022. From 2023, self-driving visits surged to 2.86 billion and then 3.21 billion in 2024, while group visits reached 0.94 billion and 1.08 billion. The gap between the two widened from 0.79 billion in 2019 to 2.13 billion in 2024.

Several factors explain the growing dominance of self-driving tourism. Private car ownership has increased rapidly, and improved rural roads make remote villages easily reachable. Self-driving travellers enjoy freedom in schedule and destination, and many prefer short trips around big cities to crowded scenic spots. Group tours, on the other hand, suffered from health concerns during the pandemic and from long-standing complaints about forced shopping and rigid schedules, which discouraged many travellers. In addition, self-driving travellers can easily explore several villages in one weekend, while group buses follow fixed routes with little flexibility.

In my view, rural tourism should adapt to the self-driving era. Villages should build parking lots, campsites, clean toilets and clear signs, and offer activities such as picking fruit, farm stays and local food experiences. Travel agencies need to redesign small, flexible and high-quality group products for elderly tourists and school trips. I predict that self-driving rural visits will exceed 4 billion by 2028, and rural tourism will become a major source of income for the countryside.

tips: 注意 2023 年光伏反超风电的关键转折点；分析两种技术增速差异的原因；结尾讨论互补关系与储能、电网等挑战。
modelAnswer:
The line chart compares the cumulative installed capacity of wind power and solar power in China from 2019 to 2024. Overall, both grew substantially, but solar power expanded far faster and overtook wind power in 2023.

In 2019, wind capacity stood at 210 GW, slightly ahead of solar at 204 GW. Wind kept its lead over the next three years, reaching 281 GW in 2020, 328 GW in 2021 and 365 GW in 2022, while solar grew to 253 GW, 306 GW and 340 GW respectively. The turning point came in 2023, when solar capacity surged by 220 GW to 560 GW, far exceeding wind's 441 GW. In 2024, the gap widened further, as solar reached 830 GW against 520 GW for wind. In just five years, solar capacity more than quadrupled, while wind capacity roughly doubled. This crossover marks a historic shift in China's clean energy landscape and signals a new phase of its energy transition.

The dramatic rise of solar power reflects falling panel prices, flexible installation on rooftops and in deserts, and strong policy support for distributed generation. Wind power has also grown steadily, but its expansion is limited by site selection, long approval procedures and the need for large equipment. Both technologies are central to China's plan to peak carbon emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060.

In my opinion, solar will continue to grow faster than wind in the coming years, but a balanced energy mix is essential. Solar produces electricity mainly during the day, while wind can generate power at night, so the two technologies complement each other. The key challenge is to upgrade grids and build large-scale storage to absorb the growing amount of clean energy. I predict that by 2030, China's combined wind and solar capacity will reach about 3,000 GW, transforming the country's energy system.

chart.title: 2019—2024 年 AI 岗位与全部岗位平均月薪对比

tips: 双系列折线图应同时描述两组数据并突出差距扩大；分析原因联系人才供需失衡；结尾给出薪资走势预测与建议。
modelAnswer:
The line chart compares the average monthly salary of AI-related positions with that of all positions in China from 2019 to 2024. Overall, both figures rose steadily, but the gap between them widened significantly over the six years.

In 2019, AI workers earned an average of 18,900 yuan per month, compared with 7,850 yuan for all positions, a gap of 11,050 yuan. AI salaries climbed to 20,600 in 2020, 22,400 in 2021, 24,100 in 2022, 25,200 in 2023 and 26,800 in 2024, an overall increase of about 42 percent. Average salaries across all positions grew more slowly, from 7,850 to 9,360 yuan, a rise of roughly 19 percent. As a result, the salary gap expanded from 11,050 yuan in 2019 to 17,440 yuan in 2024.

The widening gap reflects the severe shortage of AI talent. Companies in finance, manufacturing, healthcare and the internet are competing fiercely for experienced engineers and data scientists, and they are willing to pay a large premium to attract them. At the same time, AI skills have become the most valuable asset in the job market, because employees who master them can help companies cut costs and create new products. By contrast, growth in ordinary wages has been held back by the large supply of general workers and slower economic growth.

In my view, high AI salaries will continue in the short term, but the premium may gradually shrink as more graduates and trained workers enter the field. Universities should expand AI-related programmes, and companies should train their existing staff instead of only hiring from outside. Governments should also ensure that the benefits of AI are shared more broadly, for example through retraining programmes for workers whose jobs are affected. I predict that by 2028 the average AI salary will exceed 30,000 yuan, while the general average will approach 11,000 yuan.
